output-tile vs split-K for a whole GEMM phase in the occfuse skeleton (148 CTAs, tile order (row block, token tile, ks), CTA owns a contiguous tile range, ring of A+B slots, TMEM accumulators). KS = k splits, so the partition is output_tile at KS 1 and split_k above (equal k slices aligned to tiles; busy_ctas = CTAs with work). us = telescoping mean phase time over 112 phases incl. the barrier, median over passes. The partition table: us by (partition, ks). Stream-K (CTAs take unaligned ranges of the flattened k space) is not in this skeleton; see gemm.partition rows

note: slope over two loop lengths, 8 independent ops per iteration with addresses varying per iteration; bytes_per_clk_sm counts useful bytes (ldmatrix xN = N*128 B). Peak shared memory bandwidth is 128 B/clk/SM. rowmajor128B = 8 lanes of a phase hit the same 16B column of 8 rows of a 128B-pitch tile (8-way bank conflict); swizzle128B = chunk index xor (row mod 8), conflict-free. LDS/STS lanes read consecutive addresses (conflict-free). ldmatrix .trans only changes register layout (its checksum sums 16-bit halves: ~3 extra ALU ops per register, so .trans rows and sts.128, which builds 4 distinct values, can be issue-limited and read as a lower bound). Each iteration permutes lanes by xor (iteration mod 32) so addresses are not loop-invariant; conflict structure is unchanged. verified = checksum of loaded words (sts: read-back of last-written values)
